overview: St Nectan’s Glen is a wooded valley at Trethevy, just up the coast from Tintagel, following the Trevillet River for about a mile. Its showpiece is St Nectan’s Kieve, a waterfall around 60 feet high that pours through a hole worn in the rock into a pool below.

It has a mystical reputation: many visitors leave ribbons, crystals and little stacks of stones near the falls. The story of a 6th-century hermit saint ringing a bell here to warn ships is probably a Victorian invention, but it’s a magical spot all the same.

expect.title: The woodland walk
expect.text: Paths follow the river up through the glen to the waterfall.

expect.title: The kieve
expect.text: The waterfall and its rock arch are the highlight, especially after rain when the river is full.

expect.title: Café
expect.text: There’s a café at the site.

goodToKnow.label: Before you go
goodToKnow.text: Check the official website for opening times and entry details for the waterfall.

goodToKnow.label: Footwear
goodToKnow.text: It’s a woodland and riverside walk, so wear shoes with good grip.

week.text: An easy add-on to a Tintagel day, and a good choice on a grey or drizzly day when the woods feel at their most atmospheric. Pair it with Rocky Valley’s ravine walk next door.

pairWith.why: a dramatic ravine walk down to the sea
the legendary castle a few minutes’ drive away
a sandy cove nearby at low tide

tips: Go after a spell of rain for the fullest waterfall.
